headline: Subscription growth accelerates; cash flow cools on timing
summary_short: Bentley Systems' Q1 2026 revenue rose 14.5% y/y to $424.2M on broad subscription strength across all geographies, while operating cash flow fell 11.9% y/y to $193.4M on working-capital timing.
summary_long: Revenue grew 14.5% y/y (11.9% constant currency) to $424.2M, led by Enterprise and SELECT subscriptions with growth from existing accounts and 3% from new accounts; all three geographies grew double digits. Gross margin held near 82.6%. Opex rose 18.2% on higher headcount costs across R&D, sales, and G&A. Operating income reached $126.3M, up sharply q/q against a soft Q4 2025 base. Net income was $95.4M ($0.30 diluted EPS). Operating cash flow fell to $193.4M on working-capital timing (payables, receivables collections, Cloud Services deposits). The company repaid $678.3M of maturing 2026 Notes via Credit Facility borrowings and cash, and repurchased $40.0M of stock. No numeric FY2026 guidance was given in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Q1 2026 continued Bentley's subscription-led growth (revenue +14.5% y/y) with double-digit growth in all three geographies; cash flow softened on working-capital timing and the company repaid its maturing 2026 convertible notes using Credit Facility borrowings.

Driven by subscriptions revenue expansion from existing accounts, plus 3% growth from new accounts (led by small- and medium-sized), most notably Bentley Open Applications, Seequent, and Bentley Infrastructure Cloud; partially offset by a decline in perpetual licenses revenue.
Gross profit growth (14.9% y/y) outpaced cost of revenue growth (12.4% y/y), which rose mainly on higher cloud-related costs and headcount-related service costs per the release.

Gross profit rose $45.5M y/y while operating expenses rose $34.4M (headcount-related costs across R&D, sales, and G&A, per the release), so the larger absolute gross-profit gain lifted operating income.
